raw_response:
I am not going to spread myself too thin this year. I am old now, just two people at home, so I will keep the land mostly the way I know works: wheat on the better part of the land, then maize right after, and only a smaller piece in cotton because cotton needs too many hands. I have seen too many years to gamble. If I cut fertilizer too hard and the crop turns yellow, I lose more than I save. But money is still money, so I will not chase the highest yield either. I will use about what worked for me before, watch the weather, and irrigate when the crop really needs it because pumping well water costs cash.

For the wheat-maize land, I will keep 14 mu in the double crop. Wheat goes in around early October, same as the village usually does. I will use the same kind of seed people nearby buy, not anything fancy. Before sowing I will put most of the fertilizer down, then add some more for wheat when it starts growing strong in spring. After wheat harvest in June, I will not waste time with heavy tillage. The window is too short. I will clear the straw, make a quick pass, and plant maize right away. Maize seed I will buy hybrid seed like usual because saved maize seed is not reliable. Cotton I will keep on 6 mu only. Cotton can make some cash, but picking is tiring and costs labor, so I do not want too much of it at my age.
